structure.note: Two classes. Each Class A share has one vote and each Class B share 1/10,000 of a vote; Class B has 1/1,500 of the dividend and distribution rights of Class A, and each Class A share converts into 1,500 Class B shares. On March 4, 2026 there were 510,766 Class A and 1,390,722,404 Class B shares outstanding. The proxy says Buffett 'may be deemed to be Berkshire's controlling shareholder', but his 30.2% of the vote is below 50%, and a voting agreement makes him vote any shares above 49.9% of total voting power proportionately with other shareholders, so controlled is false under this schema's >50% test.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Sources: FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0001193125-26-083899, filed March 2, 2026) and 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001193125-26-106253, filed March 13, 2026), both read on EDGAR. LEADER: Warren Buffett was Chairman and CEO through the end of 2025; Gregory E. Abel succeeded him as CEO on January 1, 2026, and Buffett continues as Chairman (2026 proxy), so relation is 'chair'. The proxy table states his percentage of aggregate economic interest of Class A and Class B (13.7%) and of aggregate voting power (30.2%) as of March 4, 2026, so no derivation was needed. The governance section of the same proxy rounds these to 'approximately 30.0% of the voting interest and 13.7% of the economic interest'; the table figures are used. His Class A holding fell from 206,359 to 196,317 shares. Howard G. Buffett and Susan A. Buffett (his children, both directors) hold 0.2% or less of economic interest each (Susan Buffett's figure is mostly Class B held by two private foundations she votes); they are not added as a family figure because the proxy gives no family aggregate. HOLDERS left empty: the proxy gives the other large holders only as a percentage of Class B (Vanguard 11.4%, BlackRock 8.8% and State Street 5.3%, all from Form 13F reports for the quarter ended December 31, 2025). It does not give their share of total economic interest, and converting class percentages would be a derivation, so they are omitted. BUYBACKS: 0; the FY2025 cash-flow statement shows no acquisitions of treasury stock in 2025 (2024: $2,918 million). STOCK COMP: null. The FY2025 10-K has no share-based compensation expense line or note, and the proxy states the policy quoted above, but no company-wide expense figure (including any at subsidiaries) is disclosed, so 0 is not asserted. GEOGRAPHY: null. The 10-K does not report total revenue by geography; the only geographic split is insurance premiums written by region (based on the domicile of the insured), which covers one business, not total revenue.

Taxes: us-gaap:IncomeTaxesPaidNet (Note 20 by jurisdiction: U.S. federal 11,753, U.S. state 825, foreign 1,400; USD millions), down from 28,544 in 2024, when tax on large investment gains was paid. paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 10-K, accession 0001193125-26-083899). Pilot treatment (research/lenses/paidout/_pilot.json): formula with a caveat. Revenue includes 23.261bn of interest, dividend and other investment income and 11.964bn of non-cash T-bill discount accretion (paidOut excluding the accretion: 334.438bn). Insurance claims paid count as payouts. Taxes paid (13.978bn) include tax on investment gains outside revenue. Operating cash flow is after a 10.681bn non-cash equity-method impairment add-back. Capex is one line combining PP&E and equipment held for lease; the lease-fleet part cannot be split.

pay.notes: Employees: approximate year-end 2025 head count of Berkshire and its operating subsidiaries. Payroll: the 10-K discloses no group-wide staff cost, so the proxy's CEO pay ratio median for 2025 is used. Berkshire took it from a judgmental sample of about two-thirds of employees and identified the median employee at December 31, 2023 from 2023 W-2 wages and non-U.S. equivalents, saying nothing since would significantly change the ratio.
